result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would remove the evolutionary necessity of tribalism. 

Humanity’s greatest achievements stem from cooperation, but our greatest atrocities stem from our hardwired instinct to divide ourselves into "us" versus "them." Whether driven by tribe, nation, religion, ideology, or resource scarcity, this cognitive shortcut makes empathy scarce for the outsider and cruelty easy against the perceived enemy.

If that instinct were replaced with an inherent, unbreakable capacity to perceive the fundamental humanity and interconnectedness of every other person—instantly, across any divide—the mechanics of war, systemic oppression, exploitation, and cruelty would largely collapse under their own weight. 

Without the "us versus them" reflex, the remaining challenges of existence—disease, poverty, environmental stewardship—would just be problems to solve together, rather than battlegrounds for dominance.
